learn.title: Unstructured data: Blob, Data Lake and Files — cost, performance and durability
objectives: Choose between Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage (hierarchical namespace), Azure Files, Azure NetApp Files and managed disks from protocol, latency and analytics needs
Balance cost and performance with standard vs premium accounts, access tiers (hot, cool, cold, archive, smart tier), lifecycle management and reserved capacity
Pick a redundancy option (LRS, ZRS, GRS, GZRS and read-access variants) that meets durability, availability and data residency requirements at the lowest cost
Protect blob data with soft delete, versioning, point-in-time restore, immutable storage, object replication and resource locks, knowing which features need which prerequisites
Secure unstructured data with customer-managed keys, encryption scopes, private endpoints, user delegation SAS and Microsoft Defender for Storage
concepts: Hierarchical namespace (HNS)

The setting that turns a general-purpose v2 or premium block blob account into Azure Data Lake Storage. Directories become real objects, so renames and deletes are atomic, and POSIX ACLs can be set on files and folders. Blob versioning, change feed, point-in-time restore and object replication are not supported with HNS.
Access tiers

Hot, cool and cold are online tiers (millisecond access). Archive is offline and must be rehydrated first. Minimum storage periods are 30 days for cool, 90 days for cold and 180 days for archive; leaving earlier incurs a prorated early deletion charge.
Smart tier

A default account access tier (GA) that moves block blobs automatically from hot to cool after 30 days without access and to cold after 90 days, and back to hot on access. It requires a standard GPv2 zone-redundant account (ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS), never uses archive, and charges no early deletion or retrieval fees.
Lifecycle management

Free rule-based policy that tiers or deletes current versions, previous versions and snapshots based on creation, modification or last access time, filtered by prefix or blob index tags. Changes can take up to 24 hours to apply and it cannot rehydrate archived blobs.
Archive rehydration

Set Blob Tier or Copy Blob to an online tier. Standard priority can take up to 15 hours; high priority can finish in under an hour for blobs under 10 GB. Copying avoids the early deletion fee because the archived source stays in place.
Premium block blob

BlockBlobStorage account on SSD with higher capacity cost but lower transaction cost. Good for low-latency, high-transaction workloads (often above 35 to 40 transactions per second per TB). It supports LRS and ZRS only and cannot use access tiers.
Redundancy

LRS (11 nines, one datacenter), ZRS (12 nines, three or more zones, synchronous), GRS and GZRS (16 nines, asynchronous copy to the paired region). RA-GRS and RA-GZRS add read access to the secondary. Archive is supported only on LRS, GRS and RA-GRS.
Point-in-time restore

Restores block blobs in standard GPv2 accounts to an earlier state. Requires blob soft delete, versioning and change feed; its retention must be at least one day shorter than soft delete retention. It does not restore deleted containers or archived blobs.
Immutable storage

WORM protection with time-based retention (1 to 146,000 days, lock it for SEC 17a-4(f) compliance) and legal holds (until cleared). Container-level WORM works with HNS; version-level WORM needs versioning and is not supported with HNS or point-in-time restore.
Object replication

Asynchronous copy of block blobs between containers in two accounts, in any region or tenant. Requires versioning on both accounts and change feed on the source. Not supported with HNS, archived blobs or customer-provided keys.
Encryption options

All data is encrypted with AES-256 by default using Microsoft-managed keys. Customer-managed keys live in Key Vault or Managed HSM, encryption scopes apply a separate key per container or blob, and infrastructure encryption adds a second layer with a different key.
User delegation SAS

A SAS signed with a user delegation key obtained with Microsoft Entra credentials; the key is valid for up to seven days. Microsoft recommends it over service or account SAS, which are signed with the account key.
comparisons: Blob Storage vs Azure Data Lake Storage

Both are the same Blob service at the same price. Enable the hierarchical namespace for analytics engines (Spark, ABFS), atomic directory operations, POSIX ACLs, SFTP or NFS 3.0. Keep a flat namespace when you need versioning, point-in-time restore, object replication or version-level WORM.
Azure Files vs Azure NetApp Files vs Blob NFS

Azure Files gives managed SMB (SSD or HDD) and NFS 4.1 (SSD only) shares for lift-and-shift and Windows ACLs. Azure NetApp Files gives enterprise NAS with Standard, Premium, Ultra and Flexible service levels for SAP HANA, Oracle and HPC. Blob NFS 3.0 suits cheap, large-scale object data that Linux tools read as files.

Cool (30-day minimum) for data read about monthly, cold (90-day minimum) for data read rarely but needed in milliseconds, archive (180-day minimum) for data that can wait hours. Each step lowers storage price and raises access price.

Lifecycle rules give explicit control, can archive and can delete, but you design and maintain them. Smart tier needs no rules and has no early deletion fees, but works only on zone-redundant accounts and never reaches archive.
Soft delete vs versioning vs point-in-time restore

Soft delete recovers deleted blobs or containers for 1 to 365 days. Versioning keeps every prior state, including metadata changes. Point-in-time restore rolls a whole set of block blobs back to a moment in time and needs both plus change feed.
Service SAS with stored access policy vs user delegation SAS

A stored access policy (up to five per container) lets you revoke service SAS tokens without rotating the account key. A user delegation SAS avoids account keys entirely and is revoked by revoking user delegation keys or removing the signer's role.
traps: Archive is not supported on ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS accounts, and you cannot set archive as the default account tier.

Enabling the hierarchical namespace removes versioning, change feed, point-in-time restore, object replication and version-level WORM; plan protection with soft delete and container-level WORM instead.
Premium block blob accounts cannot tier data with Set Blob Tier or lifecycle management; copy data to a standard account to use cool, cold or archive.
SSD Azure file shares support only LRS and ZRS, NFS shares require the SSD media tier, and Azure Files never offers read access to the secondary region.
Point-in-time restore does not bring back a deleted container or a storage account; use container soft delete and a CanNotDelete lock.
Rehydrating with Set Blob Tier does not change the last modified time, so a lifecycle rule can send the blob straight back to archive unless it uses daysAfterLastTierChangeGreaterThan.
revision: Analytics with Spark or POSIX ACLs means Azure Data Lake Storage (enable HNS at creation).
Tiers: hot, cool 30 days, cold 90 days, archive 180 days; archive needs rehydration (standard up to 15 hours, high priority under 1 hour for blobs under 10 GB).
Unpredictable access on a zone-redundant account: smart tier. Predictable ageing or deletion: lifecycle management.
Durability: LRS 11 nines, ZRS 12 nines, GRS and GZRS 16 nines; add RA- only when the app must read from the secondary.
Point-in-time restore needs soft delete, versioning and change feed, and only works on standard GPv2 accounts without HNS.
Regulatory WORM: time-based retention policy, locked. Unknown duration: legal hold.
Prefer user delegation SAS, Microsoft Entra authorization, private endpoints and Defender for Storage malware scanning for uploads.
Reserved capacity: 100 TiB or 1 PiB units, one or three years, tied to region, tier and redundancy, standard accounts only.
